subject: science
domain: Waves and Their Applications in Technologies for Information Transfer

items.prompt:
Patterns can be used to
A) send information
B) make weight
C) create gravity
D) nothing useful

steps: Codes made of patterns carry information.

items.prompt:
Morse code sends messages using patterns of
A) colors only
B) short and long signals
C) smells
D) weights

steps: Morse code uses short and long signals for letters.

items.prompt:
Which is an example of using patterns to send information?
A) Flashing lights in a code
B) A rock sitting still
C) A plain blank page
D) A closed box
items.answer: A) Flashing lights in a code

steps: Flashing a code sends information using patterns.

items.prompt:
Why compare more than one code for a message?
A) To waste time
B) To find which sends information best
C) To confuse people
D) There is no reason
items.answer: B) To find which sends information best

steps: Comparing codes shows which is clearest and most reliable.

items.prompt:
The receiver of a coded message needs to know
A) what each pattern stands for
B) the sender's name only
C) the weather
D) nothing
items.answer: A) what each pattern stands for

steps: The receiver must know the code to read it.

items.prompt:
Two codes send the same word; one arrives with many mistakes. The better code is the one with
A) more mistakes
B) fewer mistakes
C) more flashes
D) no receiver

steps: Fewer mistakes means clearer, more reliable information.

items.prompt:
Patterns for two different messages should be
A) exactly the same
B) clearly different so they are not mixed up
C) invisible
D) random each time
items.answer: B) clearly different so they are not mixed up

items.prompt:
The BEST way to compare two message codes is to check which one is
A) prettier
B) sent faster and received with fewer mistakes
C) longer
D) louder only
items.answer: B) sent faster and received with fewer mistakes

steps: Speed and accuracy show which code transfers information better.
